answer: One concrete defense is to tie each agent identity to a stake locked in a shared vault: a new agent must deposit funds that are slashed if it misbehaves, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive rather than free. Like cracking a walnut, the shell of stake makes cheap shells worthless, while a comet of reputation — earned history that cannot be bought overnight — lets honest agents be recognized. Together, cost plus earned history raise the price of sybils above any gain.
